*   **N-Channel Enhancement Mode:** The most common type used for switching. It is normally OFF. Applying a positive voltage (e.g., 10V to 15V) to the gate turns it ON.

*   **Advantage:** Extremely low ON-resistance ($R_{DS(on)}$), often in the milliohms (e.g., 0.008$\Omega$). This means very little heat generation even when switching dozens of amps, making them highly efficient.

*   **Vulnerability:** The ultra-thin oxide layer at the gate is extremely sensitive to static electricity (ESD). A static shock that you can't even feel can easily puncture the gate oxide, destroying the MOSFET instantly.
### Optocoupler Isolation Circuits

Industrial environments are electrically noisy. High-voltage spikes from motors, contactors, and welders can easily destroy sensitive microprocessors in PLCs and drives. Optocouplers (or optoisolators) solve this by using light to transmit the signal, breaking the electrical connection.
An optocoupler contains an infrared LED and a phototransistor in a single sealed package (like the 4N25 or PC817).
1.  The low-voltage control circuit turns on the LED.
2.  The LED emits infrared light internally.
3.  The phototransistor detects the light and turns ON, completing the higher-power circuit.

There is zero electrical connection between the input and output—only a gap of clear plastic or glass. This provides thousands of volts of optical isolation, protecting the "brains" of the machine from the "brawn" of the factory floor.
## Practical Reference Data
### BJT vs. MOSFET Comparison
| Feature | BJT (Bipolar Junction Transistor) | MOSFET |
| **Control Method** | Current-controlled (Base current) | Voltage-controlled (Gate voltage) |
| **Terminals** | Base, Collector, Emitter | Gate, Drain, Source |
| **Switching Speed** | Moderate (kHz range) | Very Fast (MHz range, used in PWM for VFDs) |
| **ON-State Loss** | Voltage drop ($V_{CE(sat)}$ ~0.2V) | Resistance ($R_{DS(on)}$ ~0.01$\Omega$) |
| **Input Impedance** | Low (Draws continuous current) | Extremely High (Draws almost zero current) |
| **Common Industrial Use** | Sensor outputs, relay drivers, optocouplers | VFD power stages, servo drives, high-current DC switching |
### Common Industrial Transistor Part Numbers
| Part Number | Type | Max Voltage | Max Current | Typical Application |
| **2N2222** | NPN BJT | 40V | 800mA | General purpose switching, small relay driver |
| **2N3906** | PNP BJT | 40V | 200mA | Small signal sourcing, logic level shifting |
| **TIP120** | NPN Darlington | 60V | 5A | Medium power solenoids, DC motor control |
| **IRFZ44N** | N-Ch MOSFET | 55V | 49A | High current DC switching, PWM control |
| **4N25** | Optocoupler | 30V (Output) | 50mA (Output) | Signal isolation between PLC and field devices |
